title: Launch Corridor Blueprint: synchronized rolling windows for runtime, console, and API with capacity hedges
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Goal: Define a repeatable, cross-surface launch corridor that coordinates calendar windows for Runtime, Console, and Public API changes while minimizing customer disruption and protecting SLOs and unit costs. This blueprint produces a canonical schedule template, signal definitions, capacity-hedge playbooks, and a tested dry-run runbook for operational rehearsals.

Scope: all releases that touch runtime (inference runtime changes or kernel selection), console UX changes affecting rollout signals/dashboards, and public API surface or schema changes. Excludes purely marketing launches or client-side SDK docs updates.

Why now: We have increased cross-team coupling (runtime optimizations + console rollout + API contract changes) and recent rollouts have exposed capacity contention and unclear cutover ownership. A canonical corridor reduces negotiation friction and standardizes rollback/triggers.

Core outcomes: a) Launch corridor template (preflight windows, safeholds, and blackout lanes) published in Confluence and drive; b) Automated gating dashboard with latency/error/cost signals and run-rate forecasting; c) Capacity hedging knobs (reserved burst, model variant fallback) encoded as an ops playbook and mapped to Dedicated commitments; d) Dry-run validated with one coordinated canary across runtime/console/api before GA.

Key constraints and trade-offs considered:
- Tight windows vs. developer velocity: we propose 4-hour moving windows for high-risk launches and 24-hour ramp windows for lower-risk changes.
- Cost of reserved capacity: recommend using short-duration burst reservations (1–3 hours) tied to launch windows to reduce baseline committed cost.
- Consistency across regions: default to regional rolling windows but require a single global escalation owner to coordinate cross-region fallbacks.

Deliverables:
- Canonical calendar template (CSV + calendar-as-code metadata)
- Signal definitions doc and thresholds (latency P50/P95, inference error rate, token cost delta, KV cache miss rate)
- Capacity Hedge playbook (reserved pool config, auto-fallback mapping to quantized model variants)
- Dry-run checklist and postmortem template
- Stakeholder sign-off matrix
acceptance_criteria: Canonical launch corridor template published to Confluence and linked in the product handbook
Gating dashboard created with P95 latency, 5xx rate, token-cost delta, and KV cache miss rate signals AND alert thresholds
Capacity hedge knobs implemented in Dedicated config (burst reservations documented) and smoke-tested in staging
A dry-run executed with runtime + console + API teams and a post-dry-run retro recorded
Stakeholders (runtime, console, API, SRE, sales-ops) sign the readiness checklist before GA rollout

Define capacity hedging short-reserve flow with Dedicated billing/ops (owner: Product Ops)
Schedule dry-run and coordinate test traffic/shadowing plan (owner: PM)
Run retro and publish postmortem with action items (owner: PM)
Obtain cross-team signoff via Launch Readiness doc (owner: PM)
Update Console release flow with guardrail checks and customer-facing comms template (owner: UX)
Automate calendar-as-code sync with calendar provider and infra (owner: Infra Eng)
Document rollback criteria and automated fallback policy in runtime config (owner: ENG)
Run cost projection for hedged vs non-hedged approaches and attach to decision doc (owner: Finance)
Coordinate sales-ops comms for customers on reserved capacity that might affect SLA (owner: GTM)
Create post-dry-run action tickets and assign owners (owner: PM)
Publish a one-page launch corridor TL;DR for execs with escalation contacts (owner: PM)
Create a smoke-test GitHub PR template that includes perf/latency checks required for corridor signoff (owner: DEVEX)

retrospective_template: Post-dry-run retro: Date, Attendees, Scope executed, What went well, What didn't, Action items (owner + due date), Observability gaps, Cost surprises, Follow-ups (tickets)
communication_plan: Pre-launch: send runbook and TL;DR to stakeholders 72h before window. During launch: dedicated Slack channel #launch-corridor and SRE on-call pinned. Post-launch: 24h health check, and 72h cost & SLO follow-up. Customer comms: follow sales-ops template when reserved capacity could impact committed units.
risk_register: Risk: insufficient signal fidelity in dashboard -> Mitigation: include P50/P95 and KV cache miss by 2026-03-15
Risk: burst reservation cost exceeds projections -> Mitigation: Finance to approve cap and require PM signoff for increases
Risk: cross-region desync during rollout -> Mitigation: enforce single global escalation owner and per-region fallback policies
notes_brief: This ticket standardizes how we coordinate and execute launches that span runtime, console and API surfaces to reduce misalignment, protect SLOs, and control cost using short hedges and automated gating.
